headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write shared files and use MCP/browser tools, while pdf.js can read PDF files, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction-following loop. pdf.js processes PDF files and can run in browser contexts, making PDF content a plausible injection carrier if its output is fed into Cline. The shared filesystem bridge is documented; no stronger isolation is shown.
conditions: IF pdf.js output or extracted text is copied into Cline prompts or workspace files, injection becomes reachable.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory, malicious PDF-derived content can bridge into Cline.
mitigations: Keep pdf.js outputs in a separate folder from Cline's workspace.
Disable automatic ingestion of PDF text into prompts.
Use a manual review step before pasting any PDF-derived content into Cline.
Rename or quarantine untrusted PDFs before opening them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad filesystem read/write and browser access, and its workspace state is shared via filesystem. pdf.js reads PDF files. If sensitive PDFs are placed in the shared workspace, Cline can access them and potentially expose contents through browser or model-provider calls. The leakage path is plausible in default workspace use, though not proven uncontrollable.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are stored in the same workspace Cline can read, Cline can access them.
IF Cline sends workspace context to its model provider, PDF contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside the shared workspace.
Restrict Cline to a least-privilege workspace.
Turn off or minimize context sharing before opening PDFs.
Use separate OS accounts for the two agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem and modify git state; pdf.js can read PDF files and run browser-based tests. They overlap on shared workspace files, so concurrent edits or file rewrites can race even though pdf.js lacks write permissions. The conflict is real but narrower than a full dual-write scenario.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, Cline's writes can race with pdf.js file reads.
IF pdf.js test artifacts are written into the shared workspace by surrounding tooling, Cline may overwrite them.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Pause one agent while the other writes files.
Avoid running git operations concurrently.
Keep pdf.js artifacts read-only.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on tool outputs and modify files; pdf.js produces document-processing results that may be treated as authoritative by surrounding workflows. If Cline consumes pdf.js-extracted text without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code or commits. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Cline uses pdf.js output as source-of-truth without human verification, errors can propagate.
IF pdf.js extracts malformed text from a PDF and Cline commits based on it, downstream damage occurs.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted PDF text.
Compare extracted text against the original PDF for critical fields.
Do not let Cline auto-commit from PDF-derived facts.
Use a checksum or citation step before acting on extracted content.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between extraction and action.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and touch different data classes, so no explicit residency or certification mismatch is shown. The main compliance concern is that Cline can handle model-provider API keys and broad workspace data, while pdf.js handles PDFs locally. No PHI/EU-only flow is evidenced, so this is a limited policy-mismatch risk rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are opened in the shared workspace, retention and access policies must be checked.
IF Cline's model provider stores prompts longer than the PDF policy allows, a policy mismatch arises.
mitigations: Review retention settings for the model provider.
Keep regulated PDFs out of the shared workspace.
Document which agent may access which document class.
Disable unnecessary logging.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated files.
